1. Write only what you can verify. The email quote, dates, the process steps — each should match a document that exists. A written statement with one inaccurate claim is worse than one that says less.

---

Prior to release, I received confirmation from Dana Whitlock (AP) via email dated [date] stating the batches were "scrubbed and good to push." That email is attached as Exhibit A.

My release of the batches was based on that AP confirmation. I did not modify, override, or bypass any step in the process as it was communicated to me. I was not aware of any independent duplicate-check obligation assigned to my role at that time, and none was included in the training or process documentation I received [attach if available].

I am available to provide any further records or walk through the steps I took.

---

Notes before you submit:

- Fill in the bracketed items from records, not memory. If you can't confirm a date or batch ID in the next hour, say "approximately" or omit it.

Whether your reading was correct is the reviewer's determination, and it likely turns on what the mandate's text actually says. Read it again before your meeting — if it explicitly says the releasing officer must check independently, prepare for that; if it's ambiguous, your position has real support.
